premises.text: College recruiting is competitive and valuable, but startups/mid-size firms cannot compete with big campus spenders; students choose employers they have relationships with, while LinkedIn-style networking fails because students are poorly connected
premises.evidence_span: how can a startup or a medium-sized company compete effectively with the big guys on campus

premises.text: Campus channels meet many students at once and students stay in pipeline for years, so long-cycle relationship management is the key hiring mechanism
premises.evidence_span: once you meet students, they're going to be in the pipeline for a number of years before they take a job

premises.text: Meritful is an SRM/PaaS where companies invite ambassadors, privately connect promising students, run challenges, review student projects, and track development over years toward offers
premises.evidence_span: platform as a service for college recruiting teams to build and manage their relationship with students over multiple years

premises.text: Free for students; companies pay monthly subscription
premises.evidence_span: Meriful is always free for students and is available at a monthly subscription to companies

value.text: Growing companies hire the best university students by building multi-year relationships that big one-off campus visits cannot match
value.evidence_span: help companies hire the best students out of universities

causal_links.evidence_span: relationships are the key to hiring great students
build a sustainable relationship with students that's directly tied to their recruiting efforts
available at a monthly subscription to companies

notes: Competitive campus market, relationship-beats-brand story, and LinkedIn mismatch folded as one recruiting-problem set with long-pipeline campus features (§4.1.6). Ambassador portal, challenges, project showcase, and tracking folded as SRM cascade (§4.1.7). Private beta logos excluded as traction. ASR Meritful/Merriful/Merrifield variants left in spans. Three domains: problem, product, pricing—anti-template justified by separately revisable recruiting gap, SRM product, and subscription packaging.
